content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper describes a new method to enable interpretable learning using predefined concepts, shallow feature extractor, concept feature extractor, concept mapper and a discriminator. Due to the uniqueness of the method, authors also carried out a human-intuition study to select different parts and shape of mammal body as the key concepts and different types of scenes for classification; these result in two curated data sets for evaluate the performance of their methods. The learning objective is formulated as three components including the cross-entropy loss for classification, a similarity loss to measure the pixel-wise MSE between the original concept and visualized concept instances, and a GAN-type loss to enhance the capability of model to learn pre-defined concepts. Authors evaluated their method in terms of CRNP and accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper tackles sparsely studied territory in XAI whereas existing works either change the structure or provide post hoc explanation of a trained model. Differently, this work aims to learn a fully interpretable classifier using pre-defined concepts by human and formulate the learning problem with novel three-fold optimization objectives. Additional strength includes the curated concepts can be useful for further studies.     

The concept-based explanation (ACE) has been proposed by Kim et al 2018 and Ghorbani et al 2019 as pointed out by authors. With that in mind, it seems that the major contribution of this work is the problem formulation in Eqs 3-5 and the training scheme outlined in Figure 4.

The proposed method heavily relies on manually curated data sets such as mammal and scene concepts that is not easily transferable to other tasks and data sets. 

Finally, even the performance on these two specific tasks is not too impressive; why higher CRNP values indicate better transparency of the model (Figure 5)? Why do you show the results only on 3 out of 4 concepts (shape is not included) and why not show results on scene classification task? The concept weights on mammal classification task are not consistent with the human input, what does it indicate (Table 1)? For simple classification of 5 or 4 classes with distinct classes (Table 4), the accuracy ranging from 0.7 to 0.8 does not seem to be very promising.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The concept-based explanation (CBE) method, design, problem formulation, and training scheme are described clearly. As stated earlier, the problem formulation in three-modal learning objective appears to be novel. Unfortunately, other than that, the advantage of this method has not been clearly and convincingly demonstrated with experiments. Since this method requires manual curation and does not include source code, it is neither easy to be transferred to other tasks nor be reproduced.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposed a new concept-based explanation approach and a training scheme using curated concepts. Authors evaluated performance on two classification tasks. Whereas the problem formulation and training scheme of CBE is somewhat novel, the reviewer is concerned about performance evaluation, practical utilities, transferability, and reproducibility of this work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a method (TCNL) for incorporating concepts into discriminative models. They discuss how these concepts provide interpretability and can be ``controlled'' in a very specific sense.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
- The authors tackle an important problem and provide a straightforward running example. 
- The method proposed seems easy enough to implement.
- The notion of concept controllability has been alluded to in previous work, but it is nice to see work tackle this question directly. 

Weaknesses
- It is unclear how novel the proposed method is. See https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.07453
- The user study design could be much improved. It would be important to provide more thorough details of the experimental setup in the main text. If the concepts are preselected by the authors and then voted(?) on by the participants, wouldn't this bias the results? It would be good to discuss a scalable way to execute this user study.
- It would have been nice to see a workflow diagram of TCNL: where are the human annotators incorporated? How does controllability differ  from intervenability in concept bottleneck models.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The authors would benefit from more clear exposition that elucidates the novelty of TCNL. It's unclear why a GAN loss is used and how this provides benefits over existing methods. 
- Please provide a more concrete description on how the proposed method compares to existing methods (i.e., concept bottleneck models and their variants). I would have expected a comparison to those methods as well.
- The quality of the work is adequate, as is the reproducibility. 
- Was IRB approval sought for the user study?
- I expect more rigorous evaluation of the method on other datasets. How does the method scale with (a) the number of concepts, (b) the number of annotations per concept, (c) the quality of the GAN, and (d) the separability of the labels form the concepts.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper tackles an important problem with an interesting method; however, the execution leave the efficacy of TCNL outside of the specific setting that the authors consider. It would be useful to add additional experimentation and more clear exposition to make a stronger future submission.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
In this paper, authors propose TCNL a new approach that learns to map human defined concepts in images while simultaneously learning a classification task. 

A new dataset of concepts is introduced for mammals and scene classification which is used to train model to learn concepts in a supervised manner.

The results show that using this approach more neurons become sensitive to presence of a concept and hence the model learns better knowledge about human defined concepts. A point of concern is that although in mammal classification the proposed method improves classification accuracy , in scene classification it leads to drop in classification accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. New dataset of concepts for mammals and scene classification
2. The paper is well written, idea clearly explained

Weakness:
1. The approach needs annotations for every new concept. This makes the proposed approach not easily scalable.
2. The classification accuracy drop in Table 4 is a big concern. This could potentially be due to not identifying the most relevant scene concepts as compared to mammals where classification accuracy improves. A deeper investigation is required why accuracy drops in this case.
3. A thorough literature reviews seems to be missing e.g. one of the seminal paper "Concept BottleNeck Models" by Koh et al. is not mentioned. The idea proposed here is very similar to Koh et al. , therefore I believe the results should be compare if not quantitatively but qualitatively.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is clearly written
Quality: The quality of work and experimental evaluation is sound. It should be however compared to other papers doing similar things.
Novelty: The idea is not new and has been explored previously in several papers. The dataset and results are new.
content.summary_of_the_review: The idea and goal of the paper are worth investigating. However there are some shortcomings such as comparison to existing works with similar idea and deeper investigation of drop in classification accuracy that need to be addressed for a good score.

content.title: TCNL: Transparent and Controllable Network Learning Via Embedding Human-Guided Concepts
content.TL;DR: Propose a novel method to improve interpretability of CNN by merging concept information  corresponding to human understanding
content.abstract: Explaining deep learning models is of vital importance for understanding artificial intelligence systems, improving safety, and evaluating fairness. To better understand and control the CNN model, many methods for transparency-interpretability have been proposed. However, most of these works are less intuitive for human understanding and have insufficient human control over the CNN model. We propose a novel method, Transparent and Controllable Network Learning (TCNL), to overcome such challenges. Towards the goal of improving transparency-interpretability, in TCNL, we define some concepts for specific classification tasks through scientific human-intuition study and incorporate concept information into the CNN model. In TCNL, the shallow feature extractor gets preliminary features first. Then several concept feature extractors are built right after the shallow feature extractor to learn high-dimensional concept representations. The concept feature extractor is encouraged to encode information related to the predefined concepts. We also build the concept mapper to visualize features extracted by the concept extractor in a human-intuitive way. TCNL provides a generalizable approach to transparency-interpretability. Researchers can define concepts corresponding to certain classification tasks and encourage the model to encode specific concept information, which to a certain extent improves transparency-interpretability and the controllability of the CNN model. The datasets (with concept sets) for our experiments will also be released.
